title: Desalination permitting and financing timelines
bottleneck: In the US, the average desalination project takes 5–10 years from proposal to operation, dominated by environmental review, litigation, and financing — not construction. Plants cost around $1B, need massive capital stacks, and face community opposition over rates and marine impacts. The technology is ready, but the institutional pipeline is the bottleneck. Plants cost around $1B and need massive capital stacks, while communities oppose projects over rates and marine impacts.
why_it_blocks: Water crises unfold in years, not decades. A 10-year permitting timeline means desalination can't respond to the droughts it's meant to solve.
current_state: MENA countries build faster via state backing while Western projects stall in review. Modular off-grid units may bypass the megaproject logjam. MENA countries build faster via state backing while Western projects stall in environmental review.
